page.layout: One page of text, with margin notes in the left margin. Running head "EPISTOLA" at the top, page number "8" at top left. Main text in one column; marginal notes at left (numbers 4, 1, 2 and reference notes "Ex Timæo, & Ficino ibid. cap. 32." and "Ad Dionys.").

main_text.p: eiusque conditionem coniunctam agno4.scat, atq; ita plusculum humanitatis sapiat. Imo quod, qui natura Mathematici sunt, ad omnes reliquas artes cæteris existant longe aptiores, indicium nempe præbentes diuinioris suæ animæ, quam velpeculiari quadam præ cæteris gratia Deus in cœlis ornauerit, velqua iamantea in terris corpus aliquod nobilius inhabitauerit. Ad quam Mathescos diuinitatem hoc pacto religiose respicientes prædicti Philosophi, pueros adeoque omnes illos, quibus animum studiis applicare integrum erat, à Mathematicis exordium ducere voluerunt, tum quia iustum arbitrabantur, primitias intellectus adhuc puri synceri & vitiis nondum inquinati, (vtpote recenter admodum cœlitus demissi,) Deo animarum Mathematicarum h.e. intelligentium autori, grato animo offerre. Tum, quia animum humanum afferebant affectare qualia diuina

page.notes: Marginal notes at left: "4." beside the line "piat. Imo"; "1." beside "care integrum"; "Ex Timæo, & Ficino ibid. cap. 32." and "2." and "Ad Dionys." beside the lower lines. Exact placement of the reference marks is approximate. Spelling kept as printed, including long s rendered as s. Some words in the scan are uncertain, notably "Mathescos" and "affectare".
